angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 660,915 km at 280.07 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 3.5706 +/- 0.0373 mas (same row, RUWE 1.73): 280.07 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.95 +/- 0.15 solar radii from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-32 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract): 660,915 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.72 +/- 0.34 solar masses from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-32 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6140 +/- 95 K from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-32 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-32 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-32.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.340, rounded to two decimals
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-32 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] -0.13 dex, from Stassun et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-32 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 0.19345, from Gaia DR2 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018A&A...616A...1G/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-32 (pscomppars): age 2.22 Gyr, from Bonomo et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...602A.107B/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-32 (pscomppars): rotation period 11.6 d, from Bonomo et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...602A.107B/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-32 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 3.9 km/s, from Bonomo et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...602A.107B/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (0.95 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.941. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
